overview: The Tibetan Empire emerged as a major Central Asian power under Songtsen Gampo, controlling vast territories from the Tarim Basin to the Himalayas. It adopted Buddhism, created a writing system and competed with Tang China and the Arab Caliphate.

items.text: Songtsen Gampo marries Princess Wencheng of Tang China, who brings Buddhist images and texts.
The Tibetan writing system created based on Indian Brahmi script.
Buddhism gradually spreads, coexisting with native Bon religion.
The Jokhang Temple constructed in Lhasa, becoming Tibet's most sacred Buddhist site.
Military technology adapted from Chinese and Central Asian sources.
Controlled sections of the Silk Road, facilitating trade between China, India and Central Asia.
Diplomatic relations maintained with Tang China, Nepal and other powers.
The Tibetan script remains in use today.
Buddhism became central to Tibetan identity and culture.

fall.text: The assassination of Emperor Langdarma triggered fragmentation into competing regional kingdoms and the decline of centralized power.
